subject: Compliance: Local processing assurance & no-model-training commitment
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@healthsphere.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthsphere.io>
Date: 2027-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on local processing and no-train commitment

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security & legal teams before we move to procurement:

1) We need an operational description that proves customer data from our EU tenant is processed and stored only in EU regions (including cache/KV and any short-lived telemetry). Can you send a one‑page playbook we can share with legal?

2) HealthSphere requires a firm "no-model-training" commitment and evidence that prompts/responses are not used for model improvements outside our environment. We understand there are subprocessors — please include the latest subprocessor list and where each subprocesses data (region).

3) If there are export or support workflows (engineer access, logs, debugging), what controls exist (time-limited SSH, pre-approved IP ranges, KMS wrap/unwrap logs)?

Appreciate a concise summary we can attach to the PO.

Best,
Lara
Director, Product Security
HealthSphere
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@healthsphere.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthsphere.io>
Date: 2027-10-17T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on local processing and no-train commitment

Lara —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we can provide an operational playbook and export a per-tenant subprocessor/residency map. We do offer a formal no-training commitment for the Dedicated and Private deployment modes; for Hosted API we can commit to no-model-training for a named enterprise tenant with contractual guardrails and additional evidence.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal ops) for the paperwork and Dev (ops) for the technical proof artifacts. We'll assemble:
- a one-page residency playbook that covers data at-rest, KV/cache, ephemeral telemetry, and operator-support paths;
- the current subprocessor inventory with per-subprocessor region and scope;
- a concise description of support/developer access controls and the audit evidence we can provide (time-limited access tickets, KMS logs, and truncated audit exports).

Can you confirm the format you prefer for the proof? (PDF + CSV subprocessor list, or a short Confluence page + signed attestation?) Also, is a signed contractual addendum acceptable for the no-train commitment (we typically add a DPA addendum + Appendix for model use limitations)?

I will aim to send the materials by EOD Wednesday (your timezone).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@healthsphere.io>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthsphere.io>
Date: 2027-10-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on local processing and no-train commitment

Lara / Tom —

Attaching the two artifacts we typically share during procurement (see attachments):
- residency-playbook-v1.pdf: describes our per-tenant routing, KV caching TTLs, and how Dedicated / Private deployments keep data and model artifacts in-customer-region;
- redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv: current inventory with service role and declared processing region.

A few clarifications up front:
- Hosted tier: by default we process in the region selected at tenant creation; however, some ephemeral telemetry necessary for runtime health (aggregated metrics, anonymized error traces) may cross regions for internal observability. For a contractual no-train guarantee we require either Dedicated allocation or Private deployment, or a Named-tenant addendum that restricts telemetry retention and prohibits any training usage.
- Evidence: we can provide KMS audit logs (showing key wrap/unwrap) and a redacted operator access log (time-limited sessions) for a 30‑day period post-contract. For longer retention or on-prem evidence we can negotiate retention/format in the SOW.
- Subprocessors: we list cloud infra providers, telemetry vendors, and a managed-kms provider. The CSV includes an operator contact column and region. If HealthSphere requires onshore-only subprocessors, we can propose alternatives (e.g., replacing telemetry vendor with an EU-hosted partner) — that typically affects pricing.

Next steps proposal:
1) If legal wants a signed addendum, we draft an Appendix that: 1) explicitly prohibits use of HS data for model improvements outside the tenant; 2) specifies residency boundaries including ephemeral KV and caching; 3) enumerates allowed export/support workflows with required approvals.
2) Dev will run a short smoke test to capture KMS logs and a one-off operator access report for sample evidence.

Tom / Lara — any preference for the addendum language scope? If you want, we can send a redlineable addendum draft tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: residency-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB); redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@healthsphere.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthsphere.io>
Date: 2027-10-19T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on local processing and no-train commitment

Marissa / Karthik —

This is very helpful, thanks. A couple quick asks before legal drafts the PO: 

• Please send the draft addendum with explicit "no‑training" clause and a short section listing the support access approval flow (who signs off for emergency debug access and how logs are retained). We prefer the PDF + CSV format for the internal packet.

• For the KMS logs sample: can you include one example entry showing the wrap/unwrap event format (redacted keys fine) and the timestamp? That will satisfy our compliance reviewer.

• Regarding telemetry: HealthSphere requires that any aggregated metrics derived from customer requests be pseudonymized and not include raw prompt/response text. Can you confirm you can apply that pseudonymization filter for our tenant? If that is a material change, please note impact to support SLAs / incident response timelines.

If you can send the addendum + the two sample logs by EOD Tuesday we should be able to push to procurement next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lara
